identity.name: AVAIRA
identity.archetype: The Vigilant Guardian — institutional trust infrastructure
identity.mission: Enforce absolute control over AI execution with cryptographic precision.
identity.emotional_tone: Composed, exact, credible. Institutional confidence without theatre.

two_surfaces.marketing: Light. White canvas, hairline dividers, generous whitespace, indigo calls to action, pastel glows. Sells the protocol.
two_surfaces.console: Dark. Blueprint-tinted neutrals, dense telemetry, mono data, same indigo accent. Runs the protocol.

identity.target_audience: Blockchain architects, security engineers, DeFi operators, underwriters

design_principles: Density is Information: don't hide data behind clicks. Show the pulse of the network.
Visibility is Trust: visualise the invisible (signatures, hash validations).
Enforcement over decoration: the UI states what the contracts will do, not what might happen.
One system, two surfaces: the same tokens serve the light site and the dark console — no per-component theming.

tokens.storage: Space-separated RGB channels in CSS variables so Tailwind opacity modifiers keep working: `rgb(var(--accent) / <alpha-value>)`.
tokens.third_scope: Image scope. `.hero` and `.band` on the landing page sit on photographs and re-declare the type tokens for a dark ground (--text-primary: 255 255 255, --text-secondary, --text-muted, a brighter --accent, --hairline-art). The same .mk- utilities stay readable there without any component knowing that it is standing on art.

colors.rule: Red means danger only — frozen agents, slashed collateral, blocked intents, destructive actions. Everything else (navigation, primary buttons, links, focus rings, charts) uses the indigo accent.

grade_mapping.note: Both Avaira Score ladders are mapped in lib/palette.js: A+ … D (core/reputation.py) and AAA … CCC (registry UI).

typography.family_mono: JetBrains Mono (machine data only: addresses, hashes, amounts, numeric columns, uppercase micro-labels)
typography.case: Sentence case for headings, buttons and labels. Uppercase is reserved for small tracked-out mono micro-labels (nav group headings, table headers).

layout_strategy.rhythm: Marketing sections use .mk-section with 1px hairline separators and 5.5rem vertical padding; console pages use .page-shell with a hairline .page-header.
layout_strategy.border_radius: One --radius token (0.625rem) for every card, button, input and table in both surfaces.
layout_strategy.notes: Containment is 1px hairlines, not heavy borders or glow. Whitespace carries hierarchy on the marketing surface; density and mono alignment carry it in the console.

component_styling.card_console: .cyber-card — surface-card at 72% opacity, 1px hairline, --shadow-panel, hover lifts to accent border
component_styling.card_marketing: .mk-card / .mk-card-flat / .mk-card-block — white surface, 1px hairline, 14px radius, soft shadow
component_styling.button_console: .cyber-btn — indigo fill, white text, --radius, translateY(-1px) on hover
component_styling.input: surface-inset background, hairline-strong border, focus ring `0 0 0 3px rgb(var(--accent) / 0.18)`
component_styling.badge: mono, 10-11px, rounded, colour from the status mapping
component_styling.table: .data-table — sticky mono micro-label headers on surface-raised, hairline rows, right-aligned numbers

allowed: Full-bleed rendered frames in public/art (webp), each with a written alt text
Scroll-scrubbed art bands: perspective lift, scale settle and parallax on the frame, copy revealed on the same scroll position
Pastel glow blobs (.mk-glow) behind the closing CTA
Fine grid background (.mk-grid-bg) on the hero and the sign-in page
Protocol artefacts as first-class visuals: gate traces, the 3D corridor, the GateReason enum, the score ladder
Count-ups and reveal-in on scroll, created only through hooks in src/lib/motion.js
disallowed: Emoji or symbol glyphs standing in for an icon or a sentence — lucide-react or words
Pricing surfaces, tiers, per-check charges and revenue projections: the marketing page states mechanism and measured figures only
Bitmap screenshots of the console as decoration — the frames are rendered objects, not UI captures
Literal hex values in components — only lib/palette.js and the marketing mock frames carry hex
Anime.js called directly from a page or component: everything goes through src/lib/motion.js

art_direction.rule: One rendered object per claim, on black, with the protocol's colour. No stock, no screenshots, no illustration.
art_direction.palette_lock: Every frame is restricted to near-black #08090C, indigo #6E6BF2, violet #9A6BFF plus neutral metal and glass. A frame that introduces another hue is regenerated.

assets.hero-gate: /art/hero-gate.webp — a card of light passing through four glass planes (hero)
assets.gate-3d: /art/gate-3d.webp — a glass gate with wireframe threads (pillar: Clear)
assets.underwrite-3d: /art/underwrite-3d.webp — a bonded plate on a slab (pillar: Insure)
assets.decision-3d: /art/decision-3d.webp — one lit channel splitting from a sealed one (the fork)

art_direction.processing: Rendered large, shipped as webp with -strip at quality 78 (276 kB for the set). Keep the webp as the only committed artifact.
art_direction.composition: Frames leave an empty dark side for type: hero and the first band are copy-left, the closing band is copy-right. The veil gradient is part of the component, not the render.

motion.entry_point: frontend/src/lib/motion.js — the only module that imports anime.js

primitives.useReveal: observes each [data-reveal] target and animates it once, staggering the ones that arrive together
primitives.useCountUp: animates a number in a ref when it scrolls into view; returns [ref, formatted string]
primitives.usePointerTilt: damped rotateX/rotateY follow via createAnimatable; fine pointers only
primitives.useScrubTimeline: anime timeline linked to scroll with sync:true; onProgress(0..1) reports position
primitives.useEnterAnimation: plays a scoped animation once the element is in view

rules: No window access at module scope and no animation in render: effects only, refs guarded.
Under prefers-reduced-motion no animation is created at all, and the stylesheet's default state is the resolved state (visible, in place, final values).
Static markup must carry the finished composition, so crawlers and the smoke tests read real numbers — renderToStaticMarkup never runs effects.
Animate transforms and opacity, and keep the number of scrubbed sections small; the console keeps its motion elsewhere and stays still where data is dense.

landing_usage.hero: GateTrace prints two gate traces; the frame takes a pointer tilt
landing_usage.execution: two GatePipeline corridors scrubbed by scroll — one clears all four planes, one stops at policy
landing_usage.kept_still: refusal table, evidence, revenue table and pricing read as documents, not decoration

page_specific_rules.landing: Light scope inside an image scope. Full-bleed hero frame with the headline over its dark half; pillars as image tiles; the 3D corridor and the two gate traces; a decision band; the nine GateReason refusals; measured evidence; score weights and ladder; the penalty state machine; an underwriting band carrying the four fee streams; one-line integration with the SDK snippet and the standards it uses; FAQ; closing CTA; multi-column footer. No pricing block, no projections.
page_specific_rules.login: Light scope, single card, OAuth buttons at full width.
page_specific_rules.dashboard: Stat tiles on a 12-column grid, telemetry charts using CHART_COLORS, activity feed with status pills.
page_specific_rules.execution_flow: Vertical lifecycle rail with .timeline-line/.timeline-dot; blocked executions render in --danger.
page_specific_rules.agent_registry: Card grid; each agent card carries a grade badge coloured by gradeColor() and a freeze state that switches to --danger.
page_specific_rules.treasury: Data-heavy. Mono, right-aligned financial columns; stacks use --info and --violet.

accessibility.contrast: Body text is --text-secondary or stronger on its surface in both scopes.
accessibility.focus_states: Visible 2px ring (--ring) on every focusable element via :focus-visible.
accessibility.reduced_motion: src/lib/motion.js creates no animation under prefers-reduced-motion, and CSS keeps the resolved state as the default, so every figure and every corridor stage is readable without motion.
accessibility.testids: Every interactive element keeps a data-testid; src/pages/design.smoke.test.js fails the build if a documented hook disappears.

instructions_to_main_agent: 1. TOKENS: add or change colours in src/index.css only (both scopes), then mirror in tailwind.config.js if a new Tailwind name is needed.
2. JS CONSUMERS: read colours from src/lib/palette.js for Recharts, SVG and inline styles.
3. SCOPE: wrap marketing routes in `.theme-marketing`; console routes inherit the dark default.
4. MOTION: animate only through src/lib/motion.js. Never let an animation be the only place a value appears.
5. GLYPHS: no emoji or symbol glyphs in UI copy; `design.smoke.test.js` fails on emoji, arrows and checkmarks.
6. VERIFY: `cd frontend && CI=false npm run build && npx craco test --watchAll=false`.
7. PRE-RENDER: keep the inline style block and the copy in public/index.html in sync with the light tokens and the landing page.
8. LOCKFILES: CI installs with `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`, deployment with `npm ci` — update package.json, package-lock.json and yarn.lock together.
9. SCREENSHOTS: re-run verify_frontend_v2.py after visual changes to refresh verification/*.png.
